newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh premier says talks with Bridas deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh premier says talks with Bridas deadlocked.

text.p: Talks between Kazakhstan and Argentine's Bridas Energy Corp for the right to manage the republic's natural gas pipeline network are deadlocked, Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Wednesday.

Kazhegeldin told Reuters in an interview that Bridas, which earlier this year defeated a consortium of U.S. company Enron and Gaz de France in a tender to negotiate a contract to manage Kazakhstan's gas pipeline network for 15 years, was now offering worse conditions than initially.
"We reached an agreement and declared them (Bridas) the winners. But when we sit down to work out a contract, they start giving up their offers in principle," Kazhegeldin said.
He said Bridas had another month to improve its offer.

"We can only say at the moment that negotiations between Bridas and the Kazakh government continue," said a representative of London-based Malcolm Hurlston Consultants, a public relations agency for Bridas.

Kazhegeldin said Bridas had initially promised to pay the former Soviet republic royalties of three percent of the cost of gas transported in Kazakhstan's pipeline network but changed its offer when it was declared the winner of the tender and received an exclusive right to negotiate with the government.
"But now they say they can't pay and it's too difficult economically. But why did they promise this?" Kazhegeldin said.
He said Bridas was now offering to pay Kazakhstan royalties of 0.90 percent, while Enron and Gaz de France were offering 1.42 percent.

Kazhegeldin said the government had given Bridas one month to improve its investment offer. "You should offer us a higher royalty than that of Enron and Gaz de France, or we will be forced to give this project to them or somebody else," he said.
"If it (Bridas) does not undertake the obligations announced during the tender, we will have no moral right to agree with this," he added.
But many aspects of Bridas's offer still appeal to Kazakhstan.

Kazhegeldin said the government liked Bridas's offer to manage both the Batystransgaz pipeline network in western Kazakhstan -- which also transports Turkmen gas to Russia and Europe -- and the Alaugaz company in the south which distributes gas mainly to local consumers.
"Gaz de France and Enron wanted to get only the western pipeline network...They did not want to work with us distributing gas locally because they know that our population is insolvent," he said.
